chunks: From him, from Ayub ibn Nuhr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzahma, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever recites Surah Al-Kahf on every Friday night, it serves as an expiation for him for what is between that Friday and the next Friday."
When he wished to rebuke a man, he would say to him: "By Allah, you are more feeble than the one who leaves the Friday bath (ghusl), for he remains in purity until the next Friday."

key_terms.الْغُسْل: Ritual bath, specifically the recommended Friday bath
key_terms.سُورَةَ الْكَهْفِ: Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave), the 18th chapter of the Quran
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday night, the night preceding the day of Jumu'ah

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of reciting Surah Al-Kahf on Friday night according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the recitation of Surah Al-Kahf on Friday nights as a means of expiating minor sins (*kaffarah*) for the week. The Imam further illustrates the spiritual gravity of neglecting the Friday *ghusl* by using a rhetorical comparison, suggesting that one who omits it is more feeble than one who omits the bath entirely, as the ritual bath maintains a state of ritual purity and spiritual readiness until the subsequent Friday.
